delphi_scoring.question: Will LA06-01 be confirmed when scored against the published quantitative records?
delphi_scoring.assessor: Muse Wonder, single assessor -- provisional; a Fable/GPT/Gemini panel pass may supersede this score but may not edit the registered prediction

evidence_for.text: Wartlick et al. 2011 report the kinetics signature directly: Dpp decay length proportional to tissue width (lambda/L = 0.112, two datasets 0.107/0.116) with degradation rate falling as k ~ 1/A while production and diffusion vary only slightly.
Pentagone necessity reported independently twice: PLoS Biol 2011 (P-Mad domain stops scaling in pent nulls) and Nature 2021 (scaling fails in pent2; Pent drives scaling via binding-rate modulation).

The 2021 recycling mechanism couples the two camps mechanistically (endocytic recycling modulated by Pent changes effective transport/degradation), making a joint verdict more likely than either pure account.

evidence_against.text: The <50% pent/control slope criterion is a quantitative guess; the published effect could be real but shallower, landing the verdict at partially_resolved.

Camps may describe one mechanism at two levels (Pent-driven binding changes may BE the degradation change), risking a 'both' verdict that is true but shallow; the slope criterion is the guard against that.

delphi_scoring.resolvability_basis: All scoring records are public and quantitative (Science 2011 FRAP/gradient series; Nature 2021 extended-data scaling regressions; PLoS Biol 2011 pent time-course).

predictions.outcome_prediction: JOINT VERDICT: neither pure camp is sufficient. (i) Kinetics signature present in control discs: Dpp/PMad decay length scales with posterior compartment length (Wartlick lambda/L approximately 0.10-0.12, constant across growth) AND reported degradation rate decreases with compartment area (k ~ 1/A) while production/diffusion vary only slightly. (ii) Feedback necessity: in pentagone null (pent2) discs, the regression slope of gradient decay length against posterior compartment length falls to LESS THAN 50% of the control slope in the Romanova-Michaelides et al. dataset -- i.e. Pent loss does not merely shift the gradient, it removes its scaling.
predictions.quantitative_expectation: control lambda/L in [0.08, 0.14]; pent2/control scaling-slope ratio < 0.50
predictions.falsifier: pent2/control slope ratio >= 0.50 (feedback not necessary for scaling), OR control lambda/L outside [0.08, 0.14], OR degradation reported size-invariant (kinetics signature absent). Any one moves the verdict to refuted for the joint claim; qualitative-only support lands at partially_resolved.
